subdomain: 6.1 Conduct structured discovery and requirement gathering

en.question: A field-service company has approved the production inputs and quality criteria for invoice drafts. Discovery measures a sustained peak of 48 review-ready drafts per hour during a two-hour evening shift. Each qualified reviewer can sustainably complete 20 per hour at the accepted quality. Every invoice requires approval before release; unaccepted work may be explicitly deferred. Operations must approve a plan that prevents a growing review backlog under this peak. Which proposed arrangements are feasible on the supplied evidence? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Assign three qualified reviewers throughout the evening peak, with owned admission limits and explicit deferral if that coverage drops.
options.note: Three reviewers provide sustainable capacity of 60 per hour against the measured 48 arrivals. Coverage and admission ownership make this a feasible no-growth arrangement, not a guarantee of every individual latency target.

options.text: Assign two qualified reviewers and cap accepted arrivals at 36 per hour, explicitly deferring excess work with operations-approved notices.
options.note: Two reviewers provide 40 per hour, exceeding the capped accepted rate of 36. The stated permission to defer makes this feasible while preserving approval for every released invoice.

options.text: Assign two qualified reviewers to all 48 hourly arrivals, retaining mandatory approval and prioritizing the oldest pending invoice first.
options.note: Capacity remains 40 per hour against 48 admitted arrivals, so pending work grows by eight per hour. Oldest-first ordering changes waiting order, not the capacity shortfall.

options.text: Assign one qualified reviewer during the peak and two additional reviewers afterward, admitting all evening arrivals into the same queue.
options.note: Later staffing may clear the backlog after the peak but does not prevent its growth during the required interval. All options retain approval; this one fails the stated peak-capacity condition.
